items.title: Motorola’s Android 17 update breaks cover screen calling features for some Razr users
items.summary: Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

Motorola's Android 17 update breaks cover screen calling features for some Razr users

Making a call without unfolding your Razr just got harder.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 3:07 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Some Motorola Razr users report losing access to the dial pad and contacts on the cover screen after updating to Android 17.

• The issue appears to stem from Motorola replacing its native Phone app with Google’s, with no easy way to switch back.

• Rotating the phone or reducing the display and font sizes has helped some affected users restore the missing functionality.

One of the biggest selling points of Motorola’s Razr phones is how much you can do without ever unfolding them. We’ve previously put this versatility to the test, but something as basic as making a phone call from the cover screen is now proving difficult for some Razr owners following the Android 17 update.

Affected users say the update replaced Motorola’s native Phone app with Google’s alternative. While the new app works as expected on the main display, the cover screen experience is different. Users report that they can still access recent calls but can no longer open the dial pad or access contacts without opening the phone.

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Razr owners in a Reddit discussion say the switch to Google’s Phone app brought the welcome addition of visual voicemail, but at the expense of the cover screen dialer and full-screen calling interface. As a result, they now have to unlock their phone just to see who’s calling, instead of having the caller ID appear across the cover screen as before.

A Razr 50 Ultra (Razr Ultra 2024) owner on Motorola’s community forum describes a similar experience, saying Google’s app doesn’t scale properly on the cover screen, making it difficult to dial numbers. The user also says there’s no option to switch back to Motorola’s app through the phone’s default app settings.

Similar complaints have surfaced on the Google Play Store, where Razr owners have reported degraded functionality and poor scaling on the external display as recently as November 25. In response to one complaint, Google suggested the problem was device-specific and advised the affected user to contact Motorola.

Google Play Store

This isn’t the first time Razr owners have experienced compatibility issues with Google’s Phone app. Similar complaints date back to Android 16, but the apparent inability to switch back to Motorola’s own app following the Android 17 update leaves affected users with fewer options.

There is some good news, though. One affected owner discovered that rotating the cover screen brings back the missing Home and Dial buttons. Another recently reported success by reducing the font and display sizes under Settings > Display size & text. This suggests that at least some of the missing functionality could be down to how the app scales on the smaller display.

With Motorola’s Android 17 rollout reaching more Razr models, hopefully, Motorola and Google can iron out these compatibility issues before more owners find themselves unfolding their phones just to dial a number.

items.title: Poll: Is text selection still too finicky on Android phones?
items.summary: Selecting text on Android always feels more miss than hit.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

MobileAndroid OS

Poll: Is text selection still too finicky on Android phones?

Selecting text on Android always feels more miss than hit.

•

Nov 26, 2026 — 2:57 AM ET

•

•

Andy Walker / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

🗣️ This is an open thread.

We want to hear from you! Share your thoughts in the comments and vote in the poll below — your take might be featured in a future roundup.

This week, I encountered a Reddit post that made me feel seen. I genuinely thought I was one of the only Android users on the planet who found it incredibly tricky to highlight and copy the exact text line I need, but it appears to be a far more widespread issue.

As the Reddit post reads:

It’s such a lame part of the modern smartphone. I have asked Google about this and there is currently ‘no plans’ to improve how text is highlighted. This is so frustrating, and it’s not just an Android problem, I also have an iPhone for work and it’s even worse on that.

I couldn’t agree more.

Selecting text is a core part of the smartphone usage experience, whether it’s highlighting keywords in a website or selecting particular words to search or forward in messages.

I was a prolific Blackberry user in years past, and one of the most underrated features was the optical trackpad that appeared on several models. It allowed far more precision than modern touchscreens, and that’s the level of dexterity that many users crave today.

Android does offer users some mitigating tools to help adjust the selected text, including physically moving the cursor, adjusting it with a swipe on the Gboard spacebar, and various other gesture-based tweaks, but these actions take time. Arguably, these tools just aren’t enough.

But do you agree? Do you find it difficult to select text on Pixels, Galaxy phones, and other Android devices? How do you get around these limitations? Let’s discuss in the comments section.

Here are some more questions:

• Which apps give you the most trouble when trying to highlight or copy text?

• Do you ever use Gboard’s spacebar cursor control, the magnifying glass, or Circle to Search to grab text?

• Do you miss dedicated navigation hardware like optical trackpads and directional keys, or would you never go back?

• How would you like Google to address the text selection issues on Android if you believe there are any?

Readers' poll

items.body:
New Apple Store Opening in India, Download the Special Wallpaper Now

Wednesday November 25, 2026 8:17 pm PST by Joe Rossignol

Apple has announced it will be opening an all-new store at the Lake Shore shopping mall in Hyderabad, India on Thursday, December 10 at 5 p.m. local time.

Apple Kukatpally will be the company's first store in Hyderabad and its seventh in India.

To celebrate the store's upcoming opening, Apple has shared a special wallpaper for the Mac, iPad, and iPhone, as well as a set of stickers that can be used in apps like Messages. There is also an Apple Kukatpally playlist on Apple Music.

Tags: Apple Store, India

items.body: A MacBook Air with a new look could launch in late 2027 or 2028, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman said in the latest episode of his Power On podcast. Apple plans to refresh the ‌MacBook Air‌ with M6 chips in early 2027 alongside the MacBook Neo 2, but that update won't include a new design. A more extensive overhaul could follow later in 2027 or in 2028, and the ‌MacBook Air‌ could get an OLED display at that time. MacBook Air is Apple's most popular computer, and they need to keep it very fresh. And so my anticipation is 2027, 2028 is when we're going to get the big MacBook Air overhaul. And I think OLED will be part of that conversation. Apple last overhauled the ‌MacBook Air‌'s design in 2022, eliminating the prior wedge shape for a more uniform MacBook Pro-style chassis. The machine adopted a brighter Liquid Retina display with a notch for the camera, and a MagSafe charging port. In 2023, Apple added a 15-inch model, but since then, we've only gotten minor updates. Apple just added ‌OLED‌ to the MacBook Pro with the launch of the 2026 PROLED models, so it's not clear whether the high-end display will trickle down to the ‌MacBook Air‌ that quickly. In prior reports , Gurman has leaned more toward the 2028 timeline than late 2027. Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899, while the ‌MacBook Air‌ is one of Apple's more affordable notebooks and starts at $1,299. Apple would likely need to offer a high-end ‌OLED‌ ‌MacBook Air‌ alongside ‌MacBook Air‌ models with an LCD display to keep the price gap intact. items.title: 1Password Security Breach: What Was Accessed and What Wasn't
items.summary: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account…
items.body: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. items.title: WhatsApp Finally Adds Scheduled Messages
items.summary: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a messag…
items.body: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. items.body:
Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications

Wednesday November 25, 2026 11:58 am PST by Joe Rossignol

Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications. It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 next year.

The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details. This is just a rumor. On Android 16 and later, you can filter notifications into News, Promotions, Social, and Suggested categories, and an equivalent iOS option if implemented would help to hide advertising clutter.

items.body:
三星、SK 海力士、美光被控联手操纵DRAM价格，辩称中国厂商扩产带来竞争压力
https://unwire.hk/~
‎https://mp.weixin.qq.com/~

长鑫：啊？我压力三巨头？

quote.text: 三星、海力士、美光遭美国集体诉讼，被指借 HBM 转型操纵 DRAM 价格  诉状的核心论点在于：三星、SK海力士与美光凭借其在全球DRAM市场的寡头地位，在协同推进向HBM转型的同时，以这一战略调整为由大幅削减DDR3、DDR4等商用内存的产能，人为制造供给收缩。导致商用DRAM价格在过去四年间累计上涨约700%，对全球消费电子及商业IT采购造成广泛冲击。 ‎https://wallstreetcn.com/~

comments.text: 这一定都是阿共仔的阴谋.jpg

三家企业辩称，中国厂商正在扩大DDR4内存生产，给它们带来竞争压力，因此，逐步退出DDR4是正常的商业选择。

原告却认为，中国厂商当时所占的全球DRAM产能只有约5%，甚至更低，不足以解释三家企业几乎同时退出DDR4的决定。

更有意思的是，根据长鑫科技公开披露的材料，早在2024年底，长鑫就已经停止生产自有DDR4产品，开始向DDR5升级。而三星、SK海力士和美光，直到2025年4月至6月才相继宣布逐步退出主流DDR4生产。‎

items.title: 美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费
items.summary: 2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。 法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。 在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。 https://www.news18a.com/~ https:/…
items.body:
美国纽约州签署法案，限制汽车厂商对预装功能收取订阅费

2026年11月24日，美国纽约州州长凯西·霍楚尔签署一项编号为S.9348A/A.10411A的法案。该法案自2027年2月27日起生效，规定汽车制造商、经销商以及第三方服务提供商不得针对使用预装组件或硬件、且不会产生持续性成本的汽车功能，额外提供订阅服务或在车辆售出后收取费用。
法案将于2027年2月27日生效，违者每个销售点每次违规最高罚款250美元。

在法案签署前，汽车经销商莫霍克雪佛兰（MohawkChevrolet）总裁AndyGuelcher表示，订阅制有助于维持汽车基础售价，消费者可以按照自身需求启用部分功能。

https://www.news18a.com/~
https://www.governor.ny.gov/~

说的就是方向盘/座椅加热、通风、CarPlay之类的不联网功能
